lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northside Bakery | Delivery Driver | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Delivered morning wholesale orders to about 20 cafés and collected signed invoices.
- Loaded the van and checked each order against the dispatch list before leaving.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Made the sensor line's UART link to the test PC more reliable by raising its baud rate from 115200 to 921600.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; my findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Writes the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.

- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once while also ordering lab parts, maintaining the ESD program, training line operators and running the monthly safety walk, which raised station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
- Cut firmware update time over the air from 11 minutes to 4 by compressing images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Debounced the robot's emergency-stop input with a single 10 kOhm pull-up resistor.
- Profiling the interrupt load, moving sensor reads to DMA, splitting the control loop into fixed-priority tasks and pinning the scheduler tick, raised the controller's spare CPU from 8% to 35%.
- Presented the firmware roadmap to the hardware and product teams each quarter, and two board revisions followed its recommendations.
- Documented the bootloader and flashing process, so new engineers could flash a board on their first day.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Built a solar-powered weather station on an STM32 that reports every 5 minutes over LoRa and runs 9 days without sun.
- Cut average current from 4 mA to 1 mA, a 300% reduction, by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Raised packet delivery by 15% over LoRa, from 80% to 95% of readings, by retrying failed transmissions.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Designed the battery-monitoring board for the team's electric car, which passed technical inspection on the first attempt.
- Wrote the CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard and tested it against the motor controller before each race.
- Mentored 4 first-year members on soldering and board bring-up.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Replace the URL if it is a placeholder.
items.because: A hiring manager needs to be able to open the portfolio or code link.

items.says: Put Voltline before Clearwater Sensors and Northside Bakery.
items.because: The roles should run in reverse chronological order, with the most relevant experience first.

items.says: Give Northside Bakery less space than the engineering roles.
items.because: The role can show what you are doing now without taking space from the stronger engineering work.

items.says: Fix the `cafØs` encoding error in the first Northside bullet.
items.because: It looks like a document-export problem.

items.says: Substantiate the claim that raising the baud rate made the UART link more reliable, or distinguish reliability from speed.
items.because: The speed change alone does not establish a reliability improvement.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The Clearwater Sensors role is completed.

items.says: Clarify whether the complaint counts are per quarter before and after the procedure.
Separate the fixture and throughput result from the unrelated duties.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what caused the throughput gain, and the main achievement gets buried.

items.says: Add the measurement period or denominator for “field motor faults,” if defined.
items.because: It would make the 60% figure easier to assess.

items.says: The claim that a single pull-up resistor debounced the emergency-stop input raises technical and safety questions.
items.because: It does not demonstrate robust design.

items.says: Explain the safety architecture and your contribution if you retain the emergency-stop bullet.
items.because: The bullet does not accurately establish either one.

items.says: Fix the grammar of the opening list of actions.
items.because: It does not connect cleanly to “raised.”

items.says: Identify what “spare CPU” measures.
items.because: The 8%-to-35% result currently takes effort to parse.

items.says: Specify which recommendations influenced the two board revisions.
items.because: “Followed its recommendations” is too vague to show your contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether the nine-day runtime was measured or estimated.
The stated 300% current reduction is incorrect; 4 mA to 1 mA is a 75% reduction.
The change from 80% to 95% is 15 percentage points, not 15%.
Clarify the board’s role in passing inspection, if that link can be substantiated.
items.because: Inspection applied to the car, not solely the board.

items.says: Regroup the skills by type rather than using the current “Tools/Methods” split.
items.because: C and C++ are languages, STM32 is a platform, and oscilloscopes are equipment.

items.says: Keep C++ only if you are comfortable discussing work you have done with it.
Regroup the skills by type rather than using the current “Tools/Methods” split.
items.because: CAN is a protocol, which the current split obscures.
